 kt's Jang Jin-hyuk hits opening home run in first Korean Series start, repaying manager Lee Kang-chul's trust
 Yu Byeongmin 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.07 14:32 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ kt's Jang Jin-hyuk hits a solo home run 
 Professional baseball player Jang Jin-hyuk (33) of kt wiz, who seized his first-ever starting opportunity in the Korean Series (KS), repaid manager Lee Kang-chul's expectations by hitting a home run in his very first at-bat. 
 Starting as the second batter and left fielder in Game 4 of the KS (a best-of-seven series) in the 2026 Shinhan SOL KBO Postseason against the Samsung Lions held at Samsung Lions Park in Daegu on November 7, Jang launched a opening solo homer. 
 Facing Samsung starting pitcher Jang Chan-hee in the top of the first inning with no score and one out, Jang pulled a 144 km/h high-inside fastball on a 2-ball, 1-strike count for a 115-meter solo home run over the right-field wall. 
 It was a precious opening run that gave kt, trailing 1 win and 2 losses in the series, an early lead. 
 His batting form in previous games led to his starting nod. 
 Jang appeared as a substitute in Game 2, recording 1 hit in 1 at-bat and 1 run, and also hit a double as a pinch hitter in Game 3 yesterday. 
 After converting both of his scoring opportunities into hits, manager Lee selected Jang as a starter today instead of Kim Min-hyuk. 
 Before the game, manager Lee explained the background for starting him, saying, "Jin-hyuk's hitting timing looked good in his two previous appearances." 
 He added, "If Jang gets on base to connect with the lower-order hitters and strengthens our scoring power, we will have a good result." 
 Jang went beyond getting on base, responding with a home run that brought him home directly. 
 Jang Chan-hee, who gave up the opening home run to Jang, made his starting appearance today at 19 years, 1 month, and 2 days old, making him the second-youngest starting pitcher in Korean Series history. 
 The record for the youngest starter belongs to Lim Tae-hoon of the Doosan Bears in 2007 at 19 years, 1 month, and 1 day old.
